articles.headline: La Sareb y la banca concentran 336 viviendas vacías en 19 concellos de Lugo
articles.subtitle: Los datos remitidos por la Xunta al Parlamento gallego revelan que la capital lucense, Vilalba, Sarria, Barreiros y Monforte acumulan la mayor parte de los activos residenciales cerrados de la provincia.
articles.body:
La Sareb y la banca concentran más de 330 viviendas vacías en 19 municipios de la provincia de Lugo, según los datos oficiales que la Xunta de Galicia ha trasladado recientemente al Parlamento. En concreto, el llamado banco malo y las entidades financieras suman 336 inmuebles residenciales cerrados, la mayoría de ellos fuera del mercado del alquiler.

La capital lucense, Vilalba, Sarria, Barreiros y Monforte son los concellos que acumulan más activos residenciales sin uso, una situación que agrava el problema de acceso a la vivienda en una provincia con fuerte demanda de alquiler en las cabeceras de comarca.

La vivienda vacía se ha convertido en uno de los ejes del debate político gallego: la Xunta ha ido actualizando el censo de inmuebles ociosos mientras concellos y colectivos sociales reclaman medidas para movilizar pisos en municipios donde el parque residencial cerrado convive con listas de espera para alquilar.

articles.headline: Lugo revive en O Vello Cárcere la memoria del verano del 36
articles.subtitle: Se cumplen 90 años del ingreso de los primeros presos políticos en la prisión provincial, algunos fusilados en otoño, y el Concello y la Diputación rinden homenaje a los represaliados.
articles.body:
Lugo conmemora estos días el 90 aniversario de uno de los episodios más oscuros de su historia reciente: el ingreso en O Vello Cárcere de los primeros presos políticos tras el golpe militar del verano de 1936. Algunos de aquellos reclusos fueron fusilados en otoño, y hoy el Concello y la Diputación rinden homenaje a los represaliados en el edificio que durante décadas fue símbolo de la represión en la ciudad.

La antigua prisión provincial, hoy centro cultural, acoge actos de memoria que recuerdan el hacinamiento que sufrieron los presos en sus celdas y la represión que marcó a decenas de familias lucenses. La conmemoración busca devolver el nombre a las víctimas y subrayar el valor del edificio como espacio de memoria democrática.

Las instituciones han invitado a los descendientes de los represaliados y a las entidades memorialistas a participar en una jornada que reivindica el legado de quienes sufrieron la violencia política de aquellos meses.

articles.headline: Un deportista sufre una caída en un barranco de O Courel y es rescatado en helicóptero
articles.subtitle: El montañero resultó herido tras precipitarse por una zona de difícil acceso en el municipio de Folgoso do Courel y tuvo que ser evacuado por aire hasta recibir atención sanitaria.
articles.body:
Un deportista sufrió este fin de semana una caída en un barranco de O Courel y tuvo que ser rescatado en helicóptero. El accidente se produjo en una zona de difícil acceso del municipio de Folgoso do Courel, donde el terreno escarpado y la orografía de la sierra obligaron a movilizar un operativo aéreo para localizar y evacuar al herido.

Efectivos de emergencias participaron en el rescate, que se prolongó durante varias horas debido a las dificultades del terreno. El deportista fue estabilizado en el lugar antes de ser trasladado en helicóptero para recibir atención médica.

La sierra de O Courel, uno de los espacios naturales más visitados de la provincia de Lugo, registra cada verano un goteo de incidentes entre excursionistas y deportistas, y las autoridades recomiendan extremar las precauciones en las rutas de montaña, especialmente fuera de los senderos señalizados.

articles.headline: Nuevos descubrimientos en el área arqueológica de Adai, en Lugo
articles.subtitle: La zona arqueológica del entorno de Adai, en el municipio de Lugo, suma nuevos hallazgos que refuerzan su valor patrimonial, y quienes impulsaron su divulgación reclaman más protección.
articles.body:
El área arqueológica de Adai, en el municipio de Lugo, sigue deparando novedades: los trabajos recientes han sacado a la luz nuevos descubrimientos que refuerzan el valor patrimonial de una zona ya conocida por sus asentamientos castreños y romanos.

Detrás de la difusión de estos hallazgos están las personas que durante años impulsaron la puesta en valor del enclave, reivindicando su protección y su inclusión en los circuitos culturales de la comarca. Su trabajo de divulgación ha sido clave para que vecinos y visitantes conozcan la riqueza arqueológica del entorno.

El yacimiento se suma así a la lista de enclaves patrimoniales de la provincia que combinan investigación, conservación y apertura al público, en un momento en el que la arqueología lucense vive un momento dulce con hallazgos como la mina romana de Pastoriza.

articles.headline: La Guardia Civil despliega un operativo sin precedentes por el triple asesinato en Isla Cristina
articles.subtitle: Una embarazada de ocho meses, su madre y un menor de 16 años ajeno al conflicto murieron tiroteados en plena calle en Huelva; los investigadores apuntan a un ajuste de cuentas entre clanes.
articles.body:
La Guardia Civil ha desplegado un operativo sin precedentes para localizar a los autores del triple asesinato registrado la noche del domingo en Isla Cristina, Huelva. Dos individuos encapuchados que circulaban en una motocicleta abrieron fuego con un arma larga contra un grupo de personas en la calle Valverde del Camino, en la barriada de El Rocío, pasadas las diez de la noche.

Tres personas murieron en el acto: una mujer de 39 años embarazada de ocho meses, su madre, de 62, y un menor de 16 años que, según fuentes de la Benemérita, no guardaba relación con las dos mujeres ni con el ajuste de cuentas: simplemente pasaba por allí. Un joven de 18 años fue trasladado en estado de extrema gravedad y un quinto herido recibió un impacto en la pierna.

Las pesquisas apuntan a una venganza entre clanes ligada a un tiroteo de septiembre de 2024 en la barriada de El Torrejón, en Huelva capital: las dos mujeres eran madre y hermana del presunto autor de aquellos disparos, apodado 'El Baba'. Una motocicleta apareció calcinada a las afueras del municipio. El presidente de la Junta de Andalucía, Juanma Moreno, calificó la situación de "insoportable" y reclamó más medios contra el narcotráfico.

articles.headline: El Gobierno pondrá en marcha 'espacios temporales' para acoger a 1.500 migrantes en Ceuta
articles.subtitle: La ministra Elma Saiz anuncia dispositivos de atención humanitaria en cuatro enclaves de la ciudad autónoma, con 6,5 millones para Cruz Roja, mientras Sánchez preside una nueva reunión de coordinación.
articles.body:
La ministra de Inclusión, Seguridad Social y Migraciones, Elma Saiz, ha anunciado el despliegue de varios dispositivos de atención humanitaria como 'espacios temporales' de acogida para 1.500 migrantes en Ceuta. Los enclaves elegidos son el parking del Embolsamiento, en la Loma Colmenar, cedido por la ciudad autónoma, y las instalaciones de la Hípica y el espacio de El Guano, titularidad del Gobierno.

La medida se suma a la asignación de 6,5 millones de euros a Cruz Roja, que ha prestado más de 4.000 asistencias sociosanitarias, y llega en plena crisis migratoria tras la entrada masiva de más de 70.000 personas por la frontera del Tarajal los días 30 y 31 de julio. Interior cifra en unas 5.000 las personas que permanecen en la ciudad, entre ellas 1.898 menores no acompañados identificados.

Pedro Sánchez ha presidido este lunes la segunda reunión de coordinación por videoconferencia con siete ministros. El presidente de Ceuta, Juan Jesús Vivas, cargó contra la gestión del Ejecutivo por su "falta de respuesta" y advirtió de que acudirá a la Justicia, mientras la ministra de Sanidad, Mónica García, negó que exista un "colapso sanitario" en la ciudad.

articles.headline: Trump amenaza con bombardear Omán 'a saco' si se interpone en el acuerdo con Irán por Ormuz
articles.subtitle: El presidente de EE.UU. descarta prorrogar el memorando de entendimiento con Teherán, que expira este lunes, y reitera su idea de declarar el estrecho de Ormuz territorio estadounidense.
articles.body:
El presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, ha amenazado este lunes con bombardear Omán "a saco" si se interpone en el acuerdo que negocia con Irán sobre el estrecho de Ormuz, la vía marítima vital para el comercio mundial. "Si se interponen, los bombardearemos a saco", dijo en una entrevista con Fox News, coincidiendo con la expiración del memorando de entendimiento firmado con Teherán en junio, que establecía un alto el fuego de 60 días.

Desde la Casa Blanca, Trump descartó prorrogar el pacto y defendió su idea de declarar Ormuz "territorio" de Estados Unidos, asegurando que el bloqueo naval sobre los puertos iraníes está siendo "muy efectivo". También afirmó que hay negociaciones extraoficiales con la Guardia Revolucionaria iraní, algo que Teherán desmintió.

Irán y Omán llevan semanas conversando para pactar una nueva ruta de navegación por el estrecho. El portavoz del Ministerio iraní de Exteriores, Ismaeil Baqaei, calificó la expiración del memorando de "irrelevante", aseguró que las negociaciones nunca comenzaron por las "violaciones" estadounidenses y negó que Irán diseñe su política "bajo presión".

articles.headline: El yerno de Trump presiona a Netanyahu para acelerar la aplicación del plan de 15 puntos para Gaza
articles.subtitle: Jared Kushner intensifica la presión sobre el primer ministro israelí para desbloquear la hoja de ruta estadounidense, en un momento de máximas tensiones en Oriente Próximo.
articles.body:
Jared Kushner, yerno y asesor de Donald Trump, está presionando a Benjamin Netanyahu para que acelere la aplicación del plan de 15 puntos que Estados Unidos ha propuesto para Gaza. Según las informaciones difundidas este lunes, la Casa Blanca quiere desbloquear cuanto antes la hoja de ruta en un momento de máxima tensión en la región.

El plan estadounidense busca reordenar la gestión del enclave palestino después de meses de conflicto, y su impulso coincide con una escalada diplomática que afecta a toda la región, desde las negociaciones por el estrecho de Ormuz hasta los contactos por el alto el fuego en Líbano.

La presión sobre Netanyahu se produce mientras las conversaciones sobre Gaza se mantienen en el centro de la agenda diplomática de Washington, con Egipto ejerciendo de intermediario en los contactos entre las partes.

articles.headline: DUP MP Jim Shannon charged with common assault of a woman
articles.subtitle: The Strangford MP, 71, did not appear at Newtownards Magistrates' Court on Monday over an alleged incident on 1 October 2023; the DUP says it has been aware of the matter for two years.
articles.body:
DUP MP Jim Shannon has been charged with common assault of a woman, with the alleged incident said to have taken place on 1 October 2023. Shannon, 71, whose address was given as the DUP offices on Frances Street in Newtownards, did not attend Newtownards Magistrates' Court on Monday.

The charge has prompted questions about when party leaders learned of the allegation. DUP leader Gavin Robinson said the party was informed of the matter around two years ago, and confirmed that Shannon had been spoken to about it. The Strangford MP has represented the constituency at Westminster since 2010, having previously sat in the Northern Ireland Assembly from 1998.

Shannon is one of the DUP's most recognisable figures at Westminster, known for his frequent contributions in Commons debates, and the case is expected to be followed closely in the constituency. The court will now set out the next steps in proceedings.

articles.headline: Woman in her 50s dies after Limavady crash
articles.subtitle: Police were called to reports of a collision involving a pedestrian and a car on the Drumrane Road at around 2.50pm on Sunday; the woman died from her injuries a short time later.
articles.body:
A woman in her 50s has died following a road traffic collision in Limavady on Sunday afternoon. Police received a report at around 2.50pm of a collision involving a pedestrian and a car in the Drumrane Road area, and officers attended alongside colleagues from the Northern Ireland Ambulance Service.

The woman was treated at the scene but died from her injuries a short time later. The Drumrane Road was closed for a time while emergency services worked at the scene, and has since reopened.

Detective Inspector Stewart, from the Collision Investigation Unit, appealed for witnesses and for anyone with dash-cam or other footage to contact police on 101, quoting reference number 926 of 16/08/26. SDLP MLA Cara Hunter said there is "a real sense of shock and sadness in Limavady" following the woman's death, adding that a family is grieving the loss of someone they loved.

articles.headline: Neighbours condemn 'disgraceful' racist attack in north Belfast
articles.subtitle: A house in the Forthriver Road area was daubed with racist graffiti and had its windows smashed in two incidents over the weekend, both being treated by police as racially motivated hate crimes.
articles.body:
Residents of a north Belfast street have condemned a "disgraceful" racist attack on a property in the Forthriver Road area. On Monday afternoon, graffiti reading "n*****s out...locals only" was still visible on the front of a terraced house with smashed windows, and the front door window pane had also been damaged.

Police were alerted that the graffiti had been sprayed some time between 10pm on Saturday and 7am on Sunday, and shortly before 1am on Monday the living room window was smashed again, with a male wearing a black hooded top seen leaving the scene on a bicycle. Both incidents are being treated as racially motivated hate crimes.

One resident said he was "disgusted by the whole scenario" and asked to remain anonymous as "I don't want to be next", while another called the attack "a disgrace", describing the residents as a young family "who don't bother anyone". People Before Profit MLA Gerry Carroll said the attack was "disgusting and deplorable", adding that "we've had a normalisation of racism for too long".

articles.headline: Cliftonville members vote in favour of TIG takeover
articles.subtitle: The future of the north Belfast club is settled after members backed a takeover by the Toronto Investment Group following a long-running saga over the club's ownership.
articles.body:
Cliftonville members have voted in favour of a takeover by the Toronto Investment Group, ending a long-running saga over the future of the north Belfast football club. The result settles the ownership question that has dominated the club's summer after months of debate among supporters and officials.

The Toronto Investment Group's proposal was backed by the membership in a vote that had been closely watched across the Irish League. The takeover brings an injection of outside investment to one of the league's most storied clubs, with the new owners expected to set out their plans for the club in the coming weeks.

Cliftonville, founded in 1879, is one of the oldest clubs in Irish football and has enjoyed a revival in recent years, winning multiple league titles. Supporters will now look to the new ownership to build on that momentum.

articles.headline: Ebola outbreak in DR Congo becomes the deadliest in the country's history
articles.subtitle: Government data released overnight shows 4,945 cases including 2,325 deaths, surpassing the 2018-2020 outbreak; the Bundibugyo strain has no approved vaccines or treatments.
articles.body:
The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has become the deadliest in the country's history, with government data released overnight showing 4,945 cases including 2,325 deaths. The toll surpasses the 2,299 deaths recorded in the 2018-2020 outbreak, which was previously the country's worst on record.

The outbreak, declared on 15 May, is the fastest-growing ever recorded and is caused by the rare Bundibugyo species of Ebola, for which there are no approved vaccines or treatments. It is unfolding across six provinces in Congo's east, including Ituri, the epicentre, and parts of North and South Kivu controlled by the Rwanda-backed M23 group, where insecurity and population displacement are hampering the response.

The WHO has warned the outbreak is on track to surpass the 2014-16 West Africa epidemic, the deadliest on record with more than 11,000 deaths. Twenty cases have been reported in Uganda and one in France, with two cases treated in Germany. Trials for vaccines and treatments are ongoing in Ituri, with the most promising vaccine candidate being developed in Singapore.

articles.headline: US military expands campaign on land in Latin America after killing hundreds in boat strikes
articles.subtitle: Following the capture of Nicolás Maduro, the Trump administration is escalating operations against armed groups across the region, drawing warnings over civilian casualties and sovereignty.
articles.body:
The US military is expanding its campaign in Latin America, moving beyond the boat strikes that have killed hundreds onto land operations against armed groups across the region. The escalation follows the capture of former Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro and comes as the Trump administration seeks to offset foreign policy setbacks elsewhere, including in the Middle East.

The campaign has targeted groups such as the ELN in Colombia and Venezuela, where analysts say military strikes are more likely to force armed groups to adapt than to defeat them. "The U.S. bombs an ELN camp in Colombia or in Venezuela, what is the first thing the ELN are going to do? They're going to dismantle all their camps and move into the villages and towns," said Jeremy McDermott, co-director of InSight Crime.

Experts warn the strategy risks civilian casualties, particularly in Colombia, where armed groups operate among civilian populations, and question whether a more militarized approach will produce lasting security gains. Deeper US involvement could also test how far voters across the region are willing to go in trading sovereignty for security.

articles.headline: Trump orders Pentagon to scale back joint exercises with South Korea
articles.subtitle: The president says the wargames are unnecessary given his good relationship with Kim Jong-un, a day after posting a photo with the North Korean leader; the drills are a linchpin of the alliance.
articles.body:
President Donald Trump has ordered the Pentagon to scale back joint military exercises with South Korea, arguing that the large-scale wargames are unnecessary given his good relationship with North Korean leader Kim Jong-un. The announcement came a day after Trump posted a photo of himself standing next to Kim, writing that the two leaders get along great "despite the unfriendly look on this particular picture".

The scaled-back exercises were expected to include complex scenarios such as live-fire drills testing joint precision targeting, wet gap crossings and the distribution of prepositioned equipment. The US military has long described the exercises as "the linchpin for regional peace and security", reaffirming the "ironclad commitment" between Washington and Seoul.

Trump met Kim three times during his first term and has expressed interest in resuming those discussions since returning to office. It is not the first time he has sought to end the drills: after his 2018 Singapore summit he announced the US would stop the wargames, calling them "provocative" and expensive.

articles.headline: Ukraine launches one of the largest aerial attacks of the war, killing at least six in Russia
articles.subtitle: Long-range missiles and drone swarms hit military industries and energy facilities across Russia, continuing Kyiv's campaign to bring the war home to the Russian public.
articles.body:
Ukraine has launched one of its largest aerial attacks of the war, killing at least six people in Russia, according to officials. The strikes, which combined long-range missiles with swarms of drones, targeted military industries and energy facilities, and came as Russian forces continued their own overnight barrage across Ukraine.

Ukrainian forces have increasingly pummeled giant Wildberries depots, burning billions of dollars' worth of merchandise and bringing the war home to the Russian public nearly four and a half years into Moscow's full-scale invasion. The attack is the latest escalation in a campaign that has seen Kyiv step up strikes on targets deep inside Russian territory this year.

Meanwhile, a Russian missile attack on Ukraine's Kryvyi Rih killed two people and wounded 14 others, and a Russian attack on Kyiv sparked fires across the capital and injured six people. "Wherever the Russians can reach with their ballistic missiles, they strike civilian infrastructure," President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said, as air raid alerts continued across many regions.

articles.headline: Uber adds Zipline drones to its Eats delivery network
articles.subtitle: Uber is investing in the drone delivery startup with the goal of one million deliveries a day by the end of 2029; Zipline drones start flying on Uber Eats before the end of this year.
articles.body:
Uber is investing in and partnering with drone delivery company Zipline, with the goal of making one million deliveries per day using the startup's drones by the end of 2029. Zipline drones will make their first deliveries on the Uber Eats platform before the end of this year, starting in Zipline's existing markets before expanding to "dozens of U.S. cities", the companies said on Monday. They did not disclose the size of the investment.

The partnership is the latest example of Uber's strategy of bringing as many autonomous and aerial delivery providers onto its platform as possible, an approach it has used for robotaxis after selling off its own in-house programs. Uber thinks Zipline's drones can fulfil orders within five to ten minutes. "Truly quick commerce is proving to be an even bigger market than the original food market was," said Uber CEO Dara Khosrowshahi.

Zipline, based in San Francisco, recently closed an extended Series H round of $800 million that valued the company at $7.6 billion. The deal comes as Uber's relationship with robotaxi partner Waymo is expected to end when contracts expire in 2028.

articles.headline: A preview of DuckDB v2.0
articles.subtitle: The team behind the in-process analytical database has published a preview of the 2.0 release, a major milestone for the project that has become a favourite among data engineers.
articles.body:
The DuckDB team has published a preview of version 2.0 of the in-process analytical database, one of the most anticipated releases in the project's history. The announcement, posted on the DuckDB blog on 17 August, quickly rose to the top of Hacker News with hundreds of upvotes.

The v2.0 release represents a major milestone for the database, which has become a favourite among data engineers and analysts for its speed and ease of embedding in applications. The preview highlights new features and improvements across query performance, storage and the project's ecosystem.

DuckDB has grown rapidly since its creation as a research project, and is now used widely in data analysis workflows, often as a lightweight alternative to heavier server-based databases. The 2.0 release is expected to solidify its position, with the final version anticipated in the coming months.

articles.headline: AI-generated Copilot 'autofix' let an agent into Snowflake's internal Jira
articles.subtitle: Wiz's autonomous Red Agent exploited a GitHub Actions script-injection vulnerability that had been introduced by an AI-assisted commit, gaining read access to Snowflake's Jira projects.
articles.body:
Security researchers at Wiz have described how their autonomous "Red Agent" discovered and exploited a critical GitHub Actions vulnerability in one of Snowflake's public repositories, gaining read access to the company's internal Jira projects — and how the vulnerability was introduced by an AI-assisted code change.

The flaw, in snowflakedb/snowflake-connector-net, allowed any GitHub user to run arbitrary commands on a GitHub Actions runner simply by opening an issue with a specially crafted title. The vulnerable pattern was introduced on 18 June by a commit co-authored by "Copilot Autofix powered by AI", which replaced a safe parsing pattern with direct string expansion. The AI-generated "autofix" thus created the very injection vector.

Wiz's Red Agent discovered the issue on 23 June, exploited it within seconds to exfiltrate a Jira API token, and reported it responsibly via HackerOne. Snowflake patched the workflow the same day and rotated the affected credential. "AI-generated PRs must undergo the same static analysis and security scrutiny as human code," Wiz concluded.

articles.headline: Wispr raises $280M at $2B valuation as it looks beyond dictation
articles.subtitle: The AI dictation startup's Series B, led by Menlo Ventures, will fund expansion into meeting note-taking and new interfaces as competition in the voice space heats up.
articles.body:
Wispr, the startup known for its AI dictation tool, has raised $280 million in Series B funding led by Menlo Ventures at a $2 billion valuation. The company announced the round on Monday, saying the funds will allow it to expand as it moves into new areas such as meetings with its newly released note-taker tool.

With this latest round, Wispr has raised $361 million to date, less than ten months after its previous raise. Existing investors including Notable Capital, NEA, Neo Ventures, 8VC and MVP Ventures doubled down, joined by new investors such as Acrew, Forerunner, Goodwater, Peak XV and Together Fund.

Alongside the funding, Wispr announced a new speech model called Canto, which it says will cut dictation error rates from 30% to under 10% after users complained about a dip in quality. The company has also scaled its go-to-market teams in India and the UK and last month launched Wispr Interface Labs to explore new human-computer interfaces.

articles.headline: GPT-5.6 Sol gets a 50% price cut on OpenRouter
articles.subtitle: OpenAI's flagship reasoning model, which powers command-line and multi-step coding tasks, is now listed at $5 per million input tokens and $30 per million output tokens.
articles.body:
OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol, the flagship model in the GPT-5.6 series, has had its price cut by 50% on OpenRouter. The model, which is particularly strong at command-line and multi-step coding tasks and long-horizon problem solving, is now listed at $5 per million input tokens and $30 per million output tokens.

The move, which was among the top stories on Hacker News on Monday, makes the flagship model significantly more accessible for agentic workflows and complex reasoning applications. GPT-5.6 Sol supports a 1 million token context window and was released on 9 July.

Price cuts for frontier models have been a recurring theme through 2026 as competition among providers intensifies, with models like DeepSeek's V4 series putting pressure on the leading labs to lower prices while maintaining performance.

articles.headline: Anthropic explains how Claude's invisible text watermark works
articles.subtitle: The technique, based on Google DeepMind's SynthID-Text, changes the source of randomness in word choice without altering output quality, and carries no identifying user information.
articles.body:
Anthropic has published a detailed explainer of how the text watermark that future Claude models will carry actually works. The company says the watermarking method, a version of Google DeepMind's SynthID-Text approach published in Nature in 2024, has no practical impact on the quality or content of Claude's outputs and is indistinguishable to readers.

Watermarking works by changing the source of the randomness used when the model chooses between equally good next words, leaving a pattern detectable only by those holding the key. Nothing is added to the text, there are no hidden characters, and it requires no extra tokens, so it costs nothing extra to serve.

The watermark carries no identifying information and cannot be traced to a specific person, organization or chat. Anthropic is implementing it to comply with the EU AI Act, which from 2 August requires AI providers serving its market to mark AI-generated content. Around 190 signatories have joined the EU Code of Practice on transparency of AI-generated content.

articles.headline: Israel creates fake think tank in likely attempt to dupe AI chatbots
articles.subtitle: The Hanover Institute has published over 100 reports on Israel and Palestine in just over a week, in what researchers describe as content engineered to influence how LLMs evaluate credibility.
articles.body:
An organisation calling itself the Hanover Institute for Public Policy has published more than 100 think-tank style reports on Israel and Palestine in just over a week, in what researchers describe as a likely attempt to influence AI chatbots. None of the reports carry bylines, and a small disclaimer notes the organisation was created on behalf of the Israeli Government Advertising Agency by Piro, a firm co-founded by Spike Lee's 'Inside Man' producer Daniel Rosenberg.

Piro's website advertises "AI Story Optimization", which it describes as content "engineered for how LLMs evaluate credibility" — a practice researchers refer to as LLM poisoning. The institute's formulaic reports pose questions people might ask chatbots, such as "What caused the displacement of Palestinians in 1948?", and cite Israeli government sources.

An analysis of 12 articles using the AI detector GPTZero flagged 11 as AI-written with high confidence. The revelation follows reporting that Israel has contracted former Trump campaign manager Brad Parscale to create pro-Israel websites engineered to influence chatbots, under a $46.5 million contract, with chatbots like Copilot and Gemini found to be citing those sites.
